prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1093; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim file purposes. Can you confirm you're comfortable with that?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Great. Can you walk me through what happened on the day of the accident?

A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in Pasadena, Texas, in the right lane. The car behind me didn't stop in time and hit me from the rear. It wasn't a huge impact, but it was enough to push my car forward a bit.

Q: Were you able to drive your vehicle from the scene?

A: Yes, it was drivable, so I pulled into a parking lot nearby and waited for the police to show up.

Q: Did an officer come out and write a report?

A: Yes, an officer came out, took statements from both of us, and gave me a card with a report number on it.

Q: How are you feeling physically since the accident?

A: My neck is pretty sore, mostly in the back and on the left side. I also get a stiff feeling when I turn my head to check my blind spot while driving.

Q: Have you seen a medical provider about this?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the same day. They checked my range of motion, prescribed some muscle relaxers, and told me I had a neck strain.

Q: Have you had any follow-up treatment since then?

A: I've been going to physical therapy twice a week. It helps a little, but I still have bad days where I can't turn my head comfortably.

Q: Did you have any neck or back problems before the accident?

A: No, not that I can recall. I was active and didn't have any ongoing issues with my neck.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about the accident or your injuries?

A: Not right now. I just want to get back to normal and be able to work without pain.

Q: Thank you. We'll follow up with you once we've reviewed the information. Have a good day.

A: Thanks, you too.
